checks_run.procedure: Judge the register's disclosed residual on REQ-S12-019 ('the freshness scan reads only the newest period') with my own probe. A monthly KPI (staleAfterDays 30) has its last value, as of today minus 60 days, in the previous closed period. The current period is open and empty. Run kpi.freshness_scan. Then read how periods open (kpi.reporting_period_open).
checks_run.command: QA_PG_PORT=27905 tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh npx vitest run --configLoader runner --project integration apps/worker/test/integration/zz-domain-probe-freshness.test.ts
checks_run.environment: Clone at 60a6b3a5c; disposable PostgreSQL 16.15; the probe reuses operations-freshness.test.ts's fixtures (copy in probes/).
checks_run.expected: M0239: data that became stale opens one data_stale exception and keeps the last value with its freshness label.
checks_run.actual: Exit 1, by design: my probe's one assertion, 'M0239 expects a data.stale event: expected +0 to be 1', fails. Output: kpiFreshness={freshness:'unknown', lastValue:null, dataAsOf:null}, scan={kpis:1, stale:0, emitted:0}, 0 data.stale events. Two earlier attempts of the same probe failed on my fixture, not the product (a closed period needs closed_at; a reporting_period insert needs its audit event) and were corrected. kpi.reporting_period_open opens each period the day after it ends, so the newest open period always postdates the last value before it can become stale. The stale-data trigger is unreachable in normal operation. The register's residual is therefore a real defect, not an acceptable disclosure: F-DG6-100 (Medium). The row's literal acceptance, the connector path, passes (DOM-R1-03, DOM-R1-05, DOM-R1-10).

checks_run.actual: As built: the version comes from the newest automation_rule_enablement row at or before the event's stored outbox created_at. A 'disable' or 'backfill_disable' row, or no row, gives no candidate. r.enabled = true is still required at evaluation (the D-205 kill switch). Superseded versions may still evaluate their own events. The execution UNIQUE (rule version, trigger key) keeps one execution per rule. The D-204 and D-205 tests pass. Ticks keep the P5 behaviour. The residual race (G4: start-time stamps, so an overlapping rule transaction can make a re-evaluated envelope resolve another version) needs an overlap and a second evaluation of the same envelope. It is bounded by the evaluation lag and documented with its worst case. I accept D-203, D-204 and D-205 and the documented race as an observation. It fits M0239/REQ-S12-001 (versioned rules; automation never decides approvals) and the A13 intent (REQ-S20-013): no duplicate effects in the normal retry and replay paths, which the A13 suites prove. The race is not a finding.

F-DG6-100 (Medium, REQ-S12-019): the freshness scan reads only the newest period, and periods open automatically, so M0239's 'data becomes stale -> exception' never fires in normal operation, although the Operations screen promises it.
